pitch_detail.notes: Vertical cracks and corners, ending at a hanging belay inside a corner.
The corner starts at a mellow angle, then steepens. A wide stretch comes next, followed by a steep fingers section up to the next anchor.
An easy corner, then airy moves leftward past a block, and onward in the same direction to an anchored ledge. Protection is sparse, hence the PG13 tag.
A prominent offwidth sits left of the anchor; climb it to a friendlier crack above and belay at an anchor.

review.changed: Wrote all four pitches with stated grades and lengths. Rappelling the route or going up and right to third class is the descent; no per-station detail so no rappel table.
review.other_findings: Row grade 5.10a/b but no pitch is graded above 5.10-.

pitch_detail.notes: Start in the dihedral just right of the Goode Earth start. Twin finger cracks climb the corner; the left one is tips at first and then sustained fingers. Step left into the Green Dihedral below a block over a rubble-filled crack, take the first fingers/tight hands crack on the right side, then work up-left via a finger crack and mantle to reach the ledge under the evident offwidth.

The Wide Crack, easier than it looks and full of hidden features. It begins at #3 size, goes to #4 then #5, then pods of fingers and tight hands trend rightward into a splitter hand crack. Enter the alcove and climb to the next ledges to belay.

Low to mid fifth-class ground, mostly straight up, to a protectable 5.7 slab shared with Goode Earth. Rather than cutting right at the wide crack as that route does, go left around the bulge for a few more slab moves to a narrow ledge below a splitter .5 crack, and belay there with a .5 and nuts (at least four .5 cams if so). To avoid that crack, continue straight from the slab's end to the big comfortable ledge. A sneaky crack in the chimney's right wall takes nuts.

The .5 splitter crack gives onto a ledge: a seam and tips flare lie to the right, wide cracks and chimneys to the left. Chimney up to the fork, take the right branch, then a finger/tips crack right of the next ledge. The belay is at the bottom of a steep, yellow, lichen-covered dihedral facing right, next to a wall of stacked blocks. Belay left of the dihedral with a .75 or #1 to save small gear.
The Banana Dihedral: a curving bright yellow dihedral of tips and fingers, through the bulge and onward to a stance on the right.
Go up and around the right of the big rock pedestal, then through broken ground to a large ledge on the left.
Climb, scramble or simul-climb up and left to the ridge top.

review.changed: Wrote all seven pitches.

pitch_detail.notes: Begin at the corner base and go up to a loose ledge, cross right along it, climb a blocky, loose face crack through a big ledge and up to a smaller ledge on the left. Belay in a little corner on the face.
Discontinuous cracks up the face into blocky ground, with a good stance for the belay.
Move left from the belay and pull a small roof into the main corner. Follow the corner to a small ledge or stance.
Corner to its top, belaying near the ridge.
Blocky ridge, simply followed to its end, in about three rope lengths.

review.changed: Wrote P1-P4 and the ridge as one entry (P5-P7), as the text treats it. No grades or lengths stated for P1-P4.
review.other_findings: Text states four face pitches then ridge; row's 7 matches 4 plus 3 ridge pitches.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble ledges into a splitter hand/fist crack on a corner's left wall, get over a mini-roof, step right, and top out via a flaky corner (the tough bit) onto a large ledge with a big detached pillar.

From the ledge, head left up a loose, blocky chute, then cross the face rightward into a small belay alcove. A fixed bail anchor sits here (angle piton and a stopper with old tat); back it up with cams.

Follow a ramp slanting right, with a flared hand/fist crack, to a small shelf; traverse left, then a right-facing flake with a flared hand crack over a small bulge to a small ledge with a perched triangular block, at the base of the main upper dihedral. A bail anchor of two stoppers on cord here is unreliable.

Pass a flake bulge to enter the big dihedral and follow its corner crack until it pinches shut, forcing you into the parallel furrowed cracks of the left wall, which are offwidth for a while. This wide section is the crux. Belay on a small ledge in the corner after it ends. Bring #4 and #5, bumped and back-cleaned.
Twin hand cracks in the furrows of the left wall, then more hand crack on great rock to a good ledge.

Corner up on hand and fist cracks, left into an easier gritty system (staying right gives better, harder crack), then back right to finish on good rock in a fist crack that narrows to fingers. Ends on a big terrace where the steep part of the west face finishes. Unrope and scramble fourth/easy fifth class up and right, or simul to the top.

review.changed: Wrote all six pitches; feet converted to metres. The text calls the flaky corner on P1 and the wide section on P4 both the crux; only P4 marked, since it says crux of the route.

pitch_detail.notes: Start in a dihedral about 10 ft above the ground on the wall's left. Climb it 20 ft until gear runs out, then step right to the evident crack in the corner that faces left. Follow that crack system for nearly the whole rope: easier ground, a large right-facing corner, a step left around its edge, then juggy face holds. Bolted belay below a small roof split by an upside-down V notch.

Sustained; extend gear and bring alpine draws. Climb up and right through the notch in the roof, traverse right on the face (one bolt) to a small right-facing corner and follow it to the roofs. Pull two roofs, trending left, into a big left-facing corner (5.10a), then 5.6 buckets and jugs. Belay right above with #.75 to #1 gear.

Go straight to the foot of the conspicuous parallel-sided chimney (about 15 ft high), climb it, and leave it to the right. Trend left to a nice stance on the arete, just past a stem-box, on the buttress's left edge.
Follow the arete, which trends right throughout; protection and climbing are best right on it. Belay at the wall top before the talus field.

review.changed: Wrote the four buttress pitches the text describes. The remaining ridge pitches are not described pitch by pitch (only a mention that pitch 9 has stegosaurus-style climbing), so no entries for 5-11.
review.other_findings: Row says 11 pitches; text details only 4 plus south-ridge scrambling. Descent includes one rappel of about 80 ft, but not as a station list.

pitch_detail.notes: A gentler face, with cracks in a small corner, to a big broken ledge dotted with bushes, a comfortable belay.

The clear crack on the buttress's right side ends on a ramp right of a large block. A sketchy move left reaches the arete block, with gear in a wide crack. Then a left-hand right-facing corner with a hand crack, another exposed step to arete blocks, and a broken ledge belay.

Onto the face left of the arete with exposed moves, past disconcerting flakes. About 5 to 10 m of poor rock. Aim for the notch on the arete's left, or take the bolder line back right under a roof near the notch, then onto the arete to a belay below the final angular section. Going straight up from the belay to the roof near the notch stays on the arete but protects poorly; probably about 5.10.

Blocky, angular arete. Gear in cracks and horizontals covers the opening 5 m. The one bolt on the whole route then guards the 5.9 crux, face moves using sidepulls and knobs to another horizontal that takes gear. Easier but runout ground through the blocks gains the summit.

review.changed: Wrote all four pitches.

pitch_detail.notes: Follow the ice flow to the snow ledge. Fat ice when climbed. The anchor is bolted unless snow has covered it.

Between 165 and 230 ft. Thin mixed: crack torques, turf hooks and doubtful gear, to a snow and ice ramp below a diagonal rock band. Protection runs thin. Belay in cracks in the band when the rope ends, with steep snow in between.
A short hidden snow ramp breaches the small overhanging wall to the low-angle snow shoulder. It is a long way to solid rock for a belay, so use snow anchors or simul-climb to the rock.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches; P2 length is a range so kept in notes. This route forms rarely.

pitch_detail.notes: Short easy rock step to snow, then a much steeper rock section. Near the top, go right of a bulge over sloping rock; a small snow patch above is the belay. As hard as the upper crux, though in a different style.
Awkward move right off the belay, then easy rock and snow. The gully narrows into a chimney past a small chockstone, then a short steep snow bit below a large chimney and chockstone, where you belay.
Avoid the chimney by traversing right about 10 ft to a loose corner and ramp. Roughly 12 ft of loose, moderate drytooling in the corner, then an easy ramp and snowfield. The Access Ramp joins here.
Take the right side of the upper gully along the dihedral until you can cross left into the left-hand couloir.
The technical crux of the upper route: easy snow to a steep chimney packed with near-vertical, unconsolidated snow, a brief bout, then more snow and an easy big chockstone.
Easy snow up the couloir, bypassing a simple rock step on the left.
More easy snow with a couple of easy rock steps.
Up the couloir until it steepens and chokes, then traverse right onto a buttress and follow moderate broken ground up its right side.
A narrow gully crosses the buttress edge, trending up and slightly left to the east ridge, where the route ends.

review.changed: Wrote all nine pitches. No per-pitch grades are given. Descent is by the summit (about 800 ft more) or over the south buttress.

pitch_detail.notes: The crux, and the origin of the name; harder than it looks. Short easy snow over blocky rock to a steep rock face. Follow weaknesses straight up gray rock toward a red intrusion and a small snow patch and ledge. Water ice coated this and the next pitch once, but that is rare and not to be counted on.

Climb straight up from the ledge via a crack and chimney. You can continue in red rock or traverse left around a gray arete; take the left option on gray rock toward a blocky ramp system. Awkward ramp climbing reaches an easy snow couloir and the belay.
Up the snow couloir almost to its end, traverse left over red rock into a narrow couloir, crossing one easy rock step, to a belay at a full rope length, where a rock rib sits between two couloirs.
About 70 m. Climb the rib or either couloir, depending on snow and how easy the rib is. Simul-climbing from here to about pitch 7 is reasonable if comfortable.
About 70 m. More rib and left couloir, aiming for a deep cleft in the rock up on the left.
About 70 m. Up the narrow couloir in the cleft, past a short rock step and a couple of big chockstones. Belay under the second chockstone in a big snow cave.
Leave the cave, passing the big chockstone on the right, chimney through a hole behind it and out onto the face. Short, to reduce rope drag.
About 70 m. Up the couloir over rock bands by the easiest way; a good point to begin simul-climbing.
About 50 m. More couloir, passing rock sections as easiest, to the Northwest Ridge where the route ends.

review.changed: Wrote all nine pitches; lengths marked approximate in the text kept in notes. No per-pitch grades are given.

pitch_detail.notes: The start is up the buttress on the left of the couloir that lies just left of the one separating Torre de Mierda from the mountain; then cross left into a shallow gully. A couple rock steps lead to a 40 ft slab, the crux: thin cracks, fragile rock, and small beaks protect it well.
About 70 m. By the easiest line straight toward a rock headwall, then go rightward on a snowy ramp to the easiest crossing of the headwall, which gives onto a snow bowl.
About 70 m. Up the snow bowl up and left, avoiding rock, into another snow bowl. Pitches 2 and 3 were once simul-climbed as roughly 150 m.
Up and left again across easy rock into another snow bowl, then up and left to the rock.
Straight up the ridge by the line of least resistance through the rock.
About 50 m. Same: straight up the ridge until it joins the Northwest Ridge.

review.changed: Wrote all six pitches; approximate lengths kept in notes.

pitch_detail.notes: Start about 20 ft left of the deep red gully that the neighbouring route follows, and climb broken rock straight up. Belay after about 55 m.
Easy, to the top of the rock band and onto the snowfield. Belay where practical.
Stay on the gully's right side and go straight up the corner. Run it out as long as you can. The Access Ramp joins here.

A big chimney system towers above. Bypass the first chimney on the face just left, steep and runout but surprisingly positive and secure. Continue up gully and chimneys to a narrow squeeze chimney with a chockstone on top, and belay right before it starts.

Bypass the squeeze chimney by a seam up and left (arrow-size), then a couple of moves right to and over the chockstone. This ends the hard climbing. Beyond, an easy snow gully forks; take the right fork.
Easy snow with an occasional rock step. Stretch the pitches; simul-climbing speeds things up if confident.
More easy snow with occasional rock steps. Near the end the gully opens into a bowl; stay left.
More easy snow with occasional rock steps. Stay left to the ridge top.

review.changed: Wrote all eight pitches. Only P1 has a stated length. No per-pitch grades; the text says the first five pitches have M4 sections besides pitch 2.

pitch_detail.notes: A steep, right-leaning crack and corner system about 60 ft tall. The top is the crux: exit right to the prominent vertical cracks and up to a stance below the short offwidth.

Climb the short offwidth, with gear placed high, then escape leftward on the face, wander upward and return right to the wide crack/corner, follow it, then step right into a short wide crack ending at a platform. Some big blocks can be avoided; keep them off the belayer. Belay with a tree, a black totem, a blue TCU and a #3.

Slip left behind the tree, work up-left for a few moves, mantle up right onto a sloping ledge, step right to a thin-fingers crack, then left onto the orange and black face. Consider a #3 for the second, and the red Alien in the nice crack before the next moves. Maybe step down, go left then up to a wide crack in a right-facing corner. A pancake flake might fall on the belayer. Wide corner to the ridge.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches; feet converted (80, 70, 50 ft). Pitch grades not stated.
review.other_findings: Stored length 55 m; pitch lengths sum to about 61 m.

pitch_detail.notes: Up a thin crack on a tall flake, then continue up the crack system above, crossing the steep part at an offwidth (a #6 helps). Belay at a decent stance, from which a thin-hands crack heads up-left.
Thin-hands crack up and left; when able, step right onto a narrow ramp/crack system and follow it to the ridge.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches; no grades, lengths or anchors stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Take the angling crack to the notch in the first roof, through the roof and corner, and escape right to better orange rock before the next roof. Link gear up and slightly left to that roof, traverse hard left to the corner and pull the roof. Belay a little higher at an adequate stance in the corner.
Up the crack and corner. Above a roomy ledge, head left to the ridge, then scramble down to the left.

review.changed: Wrote both pitches; no grades, lengths or anchors stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble up and right on the pillar and flakes, traverse left at the top to a vertical crack and corner system, and make awkward moves to a small stance where a wide crack goes up and left.

Excellent cracks up a right-facing corner. Where it passes a roof and the rock worsens, move left carefully; the blocks may be loose and could hit the rope or belayer. Belay on an awkward sloping ledge at left.

Go left, then up clear hand cracks toward a pine, behind it, and up a ledge or two to the northeast ridge about halfway up its steep section. Or traverse hard left roughly 120 ft to the ridge and scramble off to the left.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches; no grades, lengths or anchors stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Start by scrambling to the alcove under the rightmost wide crack. Climb cracks to the wide crack/flake and follow it to a good stance 15 ft below a roof-capped chimney.

Into and up the chimney to the roof, crossing it on the right at a 3 inch crack. Follow the crack system to the next roof and cross it at the crack on its right. Several reasonable belay stances follow shortly after.
Angle up and right for about 80 ft, where the terrain turns blocky; another 120 ft reaches the summit plateau. A full 60 m rope length.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches; 100, 100 and 200 ft converted. No grades stated. The route has no bolts.

pitch_detail.notes: Cracks lead up-right to the pine alcove; pass behind the tree and continue via cracks, a flake and pinnacles in the system that splits the middle of the face. Belay at a roomy ledge about 15 ft under a short offwidth.

Through the offwidth, atop large well-seated blocks below the roof. Break through the roof at an odd left-facing corner, up it, and through the next roof where the corner flips to right-facing. Corner and nearby cracks on its right lead to laybacking, then the finger crack through the next roof, a strenuous layback. Poor hanging belay under a 3 inch crack where the face steepens. A #6 was used three times.

Cracks and a corner system; at the left-or-right choice below a prow, go left. A ledge system or two, then below a face of many horizontal cracks, step up right onto it and climb it. Watch for loose blocks.

review.changed: Wrote all three pitches; 100 ft pitches converted. No grades stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Start up the corner and the cracks of its right wall, continuing rightward. Where those finish, cross further right beneath a headwall to another corner facing left, with cracks, and climb it to workable ledges.

Step off a block to the wide crack, then follow it and the weakness above. Face climb through an awkward right-leaning alcove/corner system, up and right into a major right-facing corner, tiptoe up blocks to the roof, then go right to an acceptable belay.
Trend slightly left through the broad gap in the roofs. Orange rock, and maybe a right-facing corner, lead to a spacious ledge system that crosses the face at about two-thirds height.
Traverse left on the ledge, then up and back right to the upper major left-facing crack/corner system, and up it to an adequate belay under the wide section.
A crack/corner that is frequently wide; at its end, belay to the right under a slabby face.
Up the slabby face, slightly right, then along its right edge through overlaps to easier ground and trees, to the jumbled boulder field at the top.

review.changed: Wrote all six pitches; feet converted. No pitch grades stated; row grade 5.9 PG13 not copied.

pitch_detail.notes: The initial right-angling crack to where it meets the major corner system.
Climb the corner, picking around loose rock, and stop at a left-hand belay just under where the corner crosses a roof.
Cross the roof to easier terrain and belay to the right, in the broad broken gully.
Meander up the gully and the broken face above to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote all four pitches; feet converted. No pitch grades stated; row grade 5.8 not copied.

pitch_detail.notes: About 60 m. A third/fourth-class scramble of about 80 m from the big dead pine leads to a ledge with the first bolt. Climb straight up past two bolts on easy but dubious rock to a spacious quartz-covered ledge with a two-bolt station.
About 50 m. Straight up hollow flakes and moderate slab. Easy, but some gear is suspect. Two-bolt station.
About 60 m. Up the clear splitter corner crack; when it ends, left into a small crack, then a bolt on slab, small roofs, an easy slab and one more bolt to a ledge with a two-bolt station.
Short. Straight up past a couple of bolts toward the weakness in the headwall; build a gear belay at the base of an offwidth flake.

About 60 m, possibly 5.9+. The steep offwidth flake needs a #5 or #6 or is climbed unprotected; a crack or flake to its left may avoid that, and the intended line is unclear. Above, go to the saddle under the fourth-class scramble to the summit and belay from gear or a tree. A 10 m, fourth-class scramble to the top needs no rope.

review.changed: Wrote five pitches. Lengths marked approximate are kept in notes; the 80 m scramble and the summit scramble are folded into P1 and P5.
